evidence.title: Dynamic Collaborative Path Planning for Remote Assistance of Highly-Automated Vehicles
evidence.abstract: Given its increasing popularity in recent years, teleoperation technology is now recognized as a robust fallback solution for Automated Driving (AD). Remote Assistance (RA) represents an event-driven class of teleoperation with a distinct division of tasks between the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) and the remote human operator. This paper presents a novel approach for RA of AVs in urban environments. The concept draws inspiration from the potential synergy between highly-automated systems and human operators to collaboratively solve complex driving situations. Utilizing a hybrid algorithm that makes use of the Operational Design Domain (ODD) modification idea, it considers actions that go beyond the nominal operational space. Combined with the advanced cognitive reasoning of the human remote operator, the concept offers features that hold the potential to significantly improve both RA and AD user experiences.

evidence.title: Joint vehicle state and parameters estimation via Twin-in-the-Loop observers
evidence.abstract: Vehicular control systems are required to be both extremely reliable and robust to different environmental conditions, e.g. load or tire-road friction. In this paper, we extend a new paradigm for state estimation, called Twin-in-the-Loop filtering (TiL-F), to the estimation of the unknown parameters describing the vehicle operating conditions. In such an approach, a digital-twin of the vehicle (usually already available to the car manufacturer) is employed on-board as a plant replica within a closed-loop scheme, and the observer gains are tuned purely from experimental data. The proposed approach is validated against experimental data, showing to significantly outperform the state-of-the-art solutions.

evidence.title: Lateral Velocity Model for Vehicle Parking Applications
evidence.abstract: Automated parking requires accurate localization for quick and precise maneuvering in tight spaces. While the longitudinal velocity can be measured using wheel encoders, the estimation of the lateral velocity remains a key challenge due to the absence of dedicated sensors in consumer-grade vehicles. Existing approaches often rely on simplified vehicle models, such as the zero-slip model, which assumes no lateral velocity at the rear axle. It is well established that this assumption does not hold during low-speed driving and researchers thus introduce additional heuristics to account for differences. In this work, we analyze real-world data from parking scenarios and identify a systematic deviation from the zero-slip assumption. We provide explanations for the observed effects and then propose a lateral velocity model that better captures the lateral dynamics of the vehicle during parking. The model improves estimation accuracy, while relying on only two parameters, making it well-suited for integration into consumer-grade applications.

evidence.title: Modernization of the suspension system of a Toyota Camry Solara vehicle with a study of stability
evidence.abstract: У кваліфікаційній роботі магістра розглянуто модернізацію підвіски автомобіля Toyota Camry Solara з метою підвищення стійкості та покращення експлуатаційних характеристик. Проаналізовано конструктивні особливості підвіски, стан пружних елементів і їх вплив на кінематику підвіски. Особливу увагу приділено дослідженню показників стійкості автомобіля за різних умов руху та навантаження, а також їх взаємозв’язку з комфортом і активною безпекою. Обґрунтовано напрями модернізації елементів підвіски та технічні рішення, спрямовані на підвищення стійкості, керованості й комфорту руху.In the master’s qualification thesis, the modernization of the suspension of a Toyota Camry Solara vehicle is considered with the aim of improving stability and enhancing operational performance. The design features of the suspension, the condition of elastic elements, and their influence on suspension kinematics are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to studying vehicle stability indicators under various driving and loading conditions, as well as their relationship with ride comfort and active safety. The directions for suspension modernization and technical solutions aimed at improving stability, handling, and ride comfort are substantiated

evidence.title: The phenomenon of vehicle park brake rollaway
evidence.abstract:
When a vehicle is parked on a slope with hot brakes, what appears to be a sufficient parking brake action can sometimes become insufficient. When the brakes cool

down, the braking force reduces due to relaxation of the entire parking brake system, and the vehicle may start to move, leading to obvious catastrophic consequences. This phenomenon is known as vehicle rollaway. This thesis describes the problem in detail and postulates a mechanism that accounts for the occurrence of the rollaway event on vehicles using integrated rear callipers.



Different testing methods are presented that are used to investigate the propensity of a vehicle's parking brake system to rollaway. These include on-vehicle evaluations

and laboratory based measurements. A description is given of a novel dynamometer facility that was developed for this research that is capable of testing vehicle parking

brake systems for rollaway.



Two mathematical modelling techniques are presented that demonstrate how the parking brake system parameters influence the likelihood of rollaway occurring. A

finite element model was used to simulate the change in contact pressure at the frictional interface during a rollaway event. A numerical model was also used to

predict the change in torque developed by a parking brake system cooling from an initial elevated temperature. The change in clamp load at the frictional interface was

modelled using an essentially I-D quasi-static system that showed how the stiffness and the thermal properties of the system qualitatively affect the phenomenon.



The research found that rollaway does not always start with a uniform motion, but with a stick/slip motion. The likelihood of rollaway occurring was found to be directly linked to the temperature of the brake when the vehicle is parked. Rollaway can be reduced by lowering the initial temperature of the brake prior to parking. Rollaway can also be reduced by increasing the input load to the system when applying the parking brake. The research identifies the key design parameters of the brake system components whose values require close control within the real system

if rollaway is to be avoided

evidence.title: Design and Control of Toyota Camry 2021
evidence.abstract: The thesis explores the contribution of Hybrid Electric Vehicles to sustainable transportation through emission reduction and less reliance on fossil fuels. A literature review describes the major advantages of Hybrid Electric Vehicles over traditional Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles and fully electric vehicles. An extensive survey of control techniques in Hybrid Electric Vehicles is presented. The vehicle dynamics of the 2021 Toyota Camry is also assessed. Variable-structure dynamic models of conventional and hybrid vehicles are created in MATLAB to analyze their performance. Results confirm the improved fuel economy and smoother acceleration performance of Hybrid Electric Vehicles, sustaining the proposition that Hybrid Electric Vehicles are a sustainable transportation solution capable of bridging the gap between ICE and fully electric vehicles.BSc/BAMechatronical Engineerin

mechanism_map.mechanism: Event-driven remote assistance as a fallback layer — when the automated system leaves its nominal operational state, tasks are divided between the vehicle and a remote human operator whose cognitive reasoning resolves the off-nominal situation.
mechanism_map.intervention: Add an event-driven fallback to the Camry automated stop system: continuously verify the parked state (gear position, wheel speed, inclinometer) and, if motion begins while Park is commanded on a flat surface, immediately command the electronic parking brake to hold the vehicle while escalating an alert to a remote operator/owner app for cognitive verification and confirmation of the secure state.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Any unintended rollaway is caught as an off-nominal event and corrected by the fallback (automated brake application plus remote human verification), so the vehicle remains stationary when parked on a flat surface with occupants exited.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Place the vehicle on a flat surface in Park with occupants exited, simulate a park-mechanism disengagement, and verify the system detects motion within a fixed threshold (e.g., <0.5 s and <0.3 m travel), applies the electronic parking brake to a full stop, and logs the remote escalation; repeat across many trials confirming zero rollaways beyond threshold and no false triggers during normal park cycles.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: Remote Assistance (RA) represents an event-driven class of teleoperation with a distinct division of tasks between the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) and the remote human operator.

system.value: Dynamic Collaborative Path Planning for Remote Assistance of Highly-Automated Vehicles

abstract.value: Given its increasing popularity in recent years, teleoperation technology is now recognized as a robust fallback solution for Automated Driving (AD). Remote Assistance (RA) represents an event-driven class of teleoperation with a distinct division of tasks between the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) and the remote human operator. This paper presents a novel approach for RA of AVs in urban environments. The concept draws inspiration from the potential synergy between highly-automated systems and human operators to collaboratively solve complex driving situations. Utilizing a hybrid algorithm that makes use of the Operational Design Domain (ODD) modification idea, it considers actions that go beyond the nominal operational space. Combined with the advanced cognitive reasoning of the human remote operator, the concept offers features that hold the potential to significantly improve both RA and AD user experiences.

system.value: Modernization of the suspension system of a Toyota Camry Solara vehicle with a study of stability

abstract.value: У кваліфікаційній роботі магістра розглянуто модернізацію підвіски автомобіля Toyota Camry Solara з метою підвищення стійкості та покращення експлуатаційних характеристик. Проаналізовано конструктивні особливості підвіски, стан пружних елементів і їх вплив на кінематику підвіски. Особливу увагу приділено дослідженню показників стійкості автомобіля за різних умов руху та навантаження, а також їх взаємозв’язку з комфортом і активною безпекою. Обґрунтовано напрями модернізації елементів підвіски та технічні рішення, спрямовані на підвищення стійкості, керованості й комфорту руху.In the master’s qualification thesis, the modernization of the suspension of a Toyota Camry Solara vehicle is considered with the aim of improving stability and enhancing operational performance. The design features of the suspension, the condition of elastic elements, and their influence on suspension kinematics are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to studying vehicle stability indicators under various driving and loading conditions, as well as their relationship with ride comfort and active safety. The directions for suspension modernization and technical solutions aimed at improving stability, handling, and ride comfort are substantiated

system.value: Design and Control of Toyota Camry 2021

abstract.value: The thesis explores the contribution of Hybrid Electric Vehicles to sustainable transportation through emission reduction and less reliance on fossil fuels. A literature review describes the major advantages of Hybrid Electric Vehicles over traditional Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles and fully electric vehicles. An extensive survey of control techniques in Hybrid Electric Vehicles is presented. The vehicle dynamics of the 2021 Toyota Camry is also assessed. Variable-structure dynamic models of conventional and hybrid vehicles are created in MATLAB to analyze their performance. Results confirm the improved fuel economy and smoother acceleration performance of Hybrid Electric Vehicles, sustaining the proposition that Hybrid Electric Vehicles are a sustainable transportation solution capable of bridging the gap between ICE and fully electric vehicles.BSc/BAMechatronical Engineerin

candidates.mechanism: Ultrasonic pulse-echo self-localization estimates the vehicle’s position and motion relative to its surroundings, allowing the automated stop controller to detect departure from the commanded parked position and actively hold the vehicle there.
candidates.intervention: Integrate an ultrasonic self-localization subsystem into the Camry automated stop system so that, when park is commanded, any detected displacement triggers or maintains service-brake hold until the vehicle is verified stationary.

evidence_bundle.mechanism_source_span: An ultrasonic self-localized automated guided vehicle system.

constraint_set.problem_constraint: vehicle must remain stationary when parked on a flat surface with occupants exited
constraint_set.boundary_conditions: Flat, rigid, unobstructed pavement within the ultrasonic sensing envelope; adequate reflectivity and sensor calibration; park command active; normal electrical power and brake-hold authority.

candidates.predicted_effect: Post-park rollaway displacement is reduced toward zero and held at or below the calibrated brake-hold engagement threshold.
known_failure_modes: mechanism-inherent risks include weak or specular echoes from flat surroundings, sensor occlusion, acoustic interference, estimator latency or drift, and loss of brake-hold power or authority
candidates.novel_design_variable: Ultrasonic self-localization roll-detection threshold for automated brake-hold engagement.
candidates.testable_prediction: On flat, dry pavement with the vehicle placed in park and the occupant exited, measured displacement from the initially localized parked position will remain ≤10 mm over 60 s.

cemetery_block.physical_constraint: CSF turnover rate = 2.88x/day = 259 turnovers in 90 days. No membrane or affinity mechanism can overcome this. The ceiling is PHYSIOLOGICAL (CSF production rate is a constant).
cemetery_block.lesson: Before investing in any retention mechanism, check the CSF TURNOVER RATE. The turnover rate (2.88x/day) is a physiological constant that makes long-term retention physically impossible for any membrane-based mechanism.
cemetery_block.domain_terms_source: entry vocabulary: physical_constraint + reusable_lesson + mechanism_name (stopword-normalized; generic epistemic words removed)

cemetery_consumption.rule: Art. LI: negative knowledge is a state-transition mechanism — killed invariants must be capable of changing future search; a written-but-never-read cemetery is a log, not a memory

distinctness.distinctness_rule: v2 three-verdict rule (Art. XLII): the mechanism graph aggregate (node term sets + edge signatures) is the causal core; DISTINCT iff its Jaccard < 0.45; EQUIVALENT (merge) iff >= 0.8 with at most a design-knob difference (knob/parameter/synonym renames cannot independently create an invention); INDETERMINATE for boundary-regime or failure-mode deltas on an equivalent core, or cores in the ambiguous band — kept visible, never counted as distinct; every verdict records its basis

custody_records.raw_content: Given its increasing popularity in recent years, teleoperation technology is now recognized as a robust fallback solution for Automated Driving (AD). Remote Assistance (RA) represents an event-driven class of teleoperation with a distinct division of tasks between the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) and the remote human operator. This paper presents a novel approach for RA of AVs in urban environments. The concept draws inspiration from the potential synergy between highly-automated systems and human operators to collaboratively solve complex driving situations. Utilizing a hybrid algorithm that makes use of the Operational Design Domain (ODD) modification idea, it considers actions that go beyond the nominal operational space. Combined with the advanced cognitive reasoning of the human remote operator, the concept offers features that hold the potential to significantly improve both RA and AD user experiences.

custody_records.raw_content: Vehicular control systems are required to be both extremely reliable and robust to different environmental conditions, e.g. load or tire-road friction. In this paper, we extend a new paradigm for state estimation, called Twin-in-the-Loop filtering (TiL-F), to the estimation of the unknown parameters describing the vehicle operating conditions. In such an approach, a digital-twin of the vehicle (usually already available to the car manufacturer) is employed on-board as a plant replica within a closed-loop scheme, and the observer gains are tuned purely from experimental data. The proposed approach is validated against experimental data, showing to significantly outperform the state-of-the-art solutions.

custody_records.raw_content: Automated parking requires accurate localization for quick and precise maneuvering in tight spaces. While the longitudinal velocity can be measured using wheel encoders, the estimation of the lateral velocity remains a key challenge due to the absence of dedicated sensors in consumer-grade vehicles. Existing approaches often rely on simplified vehicle models, such as the zero-slip model, which assumes no lateral velocity at the rear axle. It is well established that this assumption does not hold during low-speed driving and researchers thus introduce additional heuristics to account for differences. In this work, we analyze real-world data from parking scenarios and identify a systematic deviation from the zero-slip assumption. We provide explanations for the observed effects and then propose a lateral velocity model that better captures the lateral dynamics of the vehicle during parking. The model improves estimation accuracy, while relying on only two parameters, making it well-suited for integration into consumer-grade applications.

custody_records.raw_content:
When a vehicle is parked on a slope with hot brakes, what appears to be a sufficient parking brake action can sometimes become insufficient. When the brakes cool

down, the braking force reduces due to relaxation of the entire parking brake system, and the vehicle may start to move, leading to obvious catastrophic consequences. This phenomenon is known as vehicle rollaway. This thesis describes the problem in detail and postulates a mechanism that accounts for the occurrence of the rollaway event on vehicles using integrated rear callipers.



Different testing methods are presented that are used to investigate the propensity of a vehicle's parking brake system to rollaway. These include on-vehicle evaluations

and laboratory based measurements. A description is given of a novel dynamometer facility that was developed for this research that is capable of testing vehicle parking

brake systems for rollaway.



Two mathematical modelling techniques are presented that demonstrate how the parking brake system parameters influence the likelihood of rollaway occurring. A

finite element model was used to simulate the change in contact pressure at the frictional interface during a rollaway event. A numerical model was also used to

predict the change in torque developed by a parking brake system cooling from an initial elevated temperature. The change in clamp load at the frictional interface was

modelled using an essentially I-D quasi-static system that showed how the stiffness and the thermal properties of the system qualitatively affect the phenomenon.



The research found that rollaway does not always start with a uniform motion, but with a stick/slip motion. The likelihood of rollaway occurring was found to be directly linked to the temperature of the brake when the vehicle is parked. Rollaway can be reduced by lowering the initial temperature of the brake prior to parking. Rollaway can also be reduced by increasing the input load to the system when applying the parking brake. The research identifies the key design parameters of the brake system components whose values require close control within the real system

if rollaway is to be avoided

custody_records.raw_content: The thesis explores the contribution of Hybrid Electric Vehicles to sustainable transportation through emission reduction and less reliance on fossil fuels. A literature review describes the major advantages of Hybrid Electric Vehicles over traditional Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles and fully electric vehicles. An extensive survey of control techniques in Hybrid Electric Vehicles is presented. The vehicle dynamics of the 2021 Toyota Camry is also assessed. Variable-structure dynamic models of conventional and hybrid vehicles are created in MATLAB to analyze their performance. Results confirm the improved fuel economy and smoother acceleration performance of Hybrid Electric Vehicles, sustaining the proposition that Hybrid Electric Vehicles are a sustainable transportation solution capable of bridging the gap between ICE and fully electric vehicles.BSc/BAMechatronical Engineerin
